abstract: Diploid genomes carry millions of heterozygous variants in cis-regulatory DNA, yet most genes produce similar RNA output from two parental alleles. How this balance is maintained is unclear. We developed Nanopore-HiChIP, a long-read method that maps high-order enhancer hubs on each haplotype. Over half of these enhancer hubs differ in chromatin architecture and transcription-factor occupancy between homologous chromosomes, but their target genes show substantially lower rates of allele-specific expression than genes lacking hub regulation. Single-cell kinetic modeling shows that burst frequency and burst size change in opposite directions, thereby preserving balanced transcriptional output. This hub-mediated kinetic buffering is enriched at haploinsufficient genes and coincides with smaller effects of expression quantitative trait loci. Enhancer hubs therefore absorb allelic regulatory variation through kinetic compensation, protecting dosage-sensitive transcription.
